cards.explanation: The answer is in the morning. David says, "In the morning, O LORD, You hear my voice…" (Psalm 5:3). Then he adds, "at daybreak I lay my plea before You and wait in expectation." Morning and daybreak both show up in that one verse, friends.

The answer is True. David says, "at daybreak I lay my plea before You and wait in expectation." (Psalm 5:3). Two steps: he lays out his plea, then he waits. It's a lot like putting a tray in the oven and not opening the door every four seconds. I still haven't mastered that part.

The answer is False. David says God is not a God who delights in wickedness, and "no evil can dwell with You." (Psalm 5:4). That word "no" doesn't leave any gaps, friends. David says none can dwell with Him.

The answer is the man of bloodshed and deceit. David says, "the LORD abhors the man of bloodshed and deceit." (Psalm 5:6). Right before that he says God destroys those who tell lies. David isn't listing people God dislikes for no reason, friends. He's naming violence and lies.

The answer is the great love God shows him. David says, "…I will enter Your house by the abundance of Your loving devotion…" (Psalm 5:7). Notice whose love it is, bakers. It's God's love that gets him in, not David's résumé. That's good news for anyone who has ever shown up with a messy apron.

The answer is the LORD's way. David prays, "make straight Your way before me." (Psalm 5:8). He's asking for God's way to be clear in front of him, not his own. When you know the road is God's, friends, you can walk it with a lot less squinting.

The answer is False. David doesn't say most of their words can be trusted. He says, "…not a word they speak can be trusted…" (Psalm 5:9). Not most, not half, not one. Nothing in the verse leaves a single word standing, friends.

The answer is that they have rebelled against God. David asks God to drive them out "…for their many transgressions, for they have rebelled against You." (Psalm 5:10). The reason he gives, friends, is that they rebelled against God. He doesn't point to something they did to him.

The answer is shelter. David prays, "May You shelter them, that those who love Your name may rejoice in You." (Psalm 5:11). It's a request, friends, and "shelter" is the word he picks for those who take refuge in God. It's a cozy word, like a warm kitchen on a cold night.

The answer is shield. David says, "You surround them with the shield of Your favor." (Psalm 5:12). A shield goes all the way around here, bakers, and it's made of God's favor. That's about the best armor a person could ask for.
